source_text:
• RPG Context and Healing : Before proceeding, the group clarified that Asterius could heal a wound via a healer's intervention, but natural healing would occur later after resting ( 00:05:31 ). Lara Triglia joined the session late due to illness, and it was noted that Latis was also absent for health reasons ( 00:17:34 ) (00:45:44 ).

• Army Morale and Roleplay : Enrico America successfully used a necklace of ears to boost the morale of the army ( 00:20:13 ). Pietro Gravino attempted to raise morale further by singing about bravery and valor, invoking a passion to receive a bonus on the performance roll ( 00:25:09 ).

• Succession of the Kingdom of Salt : Pietro Gravino revealed they are the Queen of Salt following the death of their husband, Halt ( 00:33:25 ). This announcement was met with surprise and support, with Tamura officially confirming their pregnancy during the discussion ( 00:26:37 ) (00:52:36 ).

• Prisoner Management : The group discussed the status of a captured knight, with Pablo Barros noting that the ransom for such a knight is typically around 100 pounds (00:30:47 ). The group considered the logistics of custody, including the responsibility of providing for the captive’s safety, noting that maintaining a knight and squire costs approximately two pounds per year ( 00:31:58 ).

• Allegiance to King Arthur : The group presented themselves to King Arthur to reaffirm their loyalty and explain the situation regarding the Kingdom of Salt (00:34:43 ). Pietro Gravino pledged allegiance to Arthur and was officially recognized as the Queen of Salt under Arthur's vassalage, a public ceremony that secured the support of the knights of Salt ( 00:38:39 ).

• Battle Strategy : The group planned the strategy for the upcoming fight against the archers of Cambria ( 00:43:00 ). The proposed plan involves using pikemen to resist enemy knights while the group's own knights charge the archers to neutralize them, subsequently regrouping to attack the remaining enemy cavalry ( 00:44:17 ) (00:50:14 ).

• Merlin's Absence : King Arthur informed the group that Merlin had traveled to convince King Ban of Wales, the last pagan king, to join their side, though there had been no update. Pietro Gravino stated that Merlin historically arrives exactly when they intend to ( 00:45:44 ) (00:48:50 ).

• Battle Skills and Leadership : The group learned that the "battle" skill is useful for determining opportunity encounters and that the designated leader makes final decisions regarding strategy and retreats, though they may consult the group (00:51:28 ).

• Gear Updates : Before resting, the group updated their character sheets with equipment ( 00:54:03 ). Enrico America requested an additional great ax, Pietro Gravino obtained a longbow from the armory, and Asterius requested a one -handed spear (00:55:18 ).

• Weapon Rules and Interface Navigation : Pablo Barros confirmed that two -handed weapons, such as spears, are allowed for combat, while other two -handed options are limited. Regarding the interface, Pablo Barros directed the participants to the actors tab where the Day 2 battle card is located t o proceed with the encounter (00:59:04 ).

• Impassioning Mechanics : Pablo Barros explained the process of rolling for passion to gain a bonus for the day's battle. If a player succeeds on their passion roll, they receive a plus 5 bonus to every roll; if they fail, they receive a minus 5 penalty (01:00:23 ) (01:03:46 ). Pietro Gravino inquired whether they must roll again if they are already impassioned, to which Pablo Barros clarified that the bonus persists for those already impassioned, but others must choose whether to attempt the roll now or later (01:01:38 ).

• Initial Morale Calculation : Pablo Barros introduced the requirement to define initial morale by choosing a passion, with the final morale value determined by the average of everyone's chosen passion scores. Enrico America, Pietro Gravino, and Laura Triglia selected their respective  passions, including love for family, homage to Lord, and hate for the Picts, resulting in an initial morale score of 13 ( 01:04:58 ). Pablo Barros emphasized that morale is critical because encounters have minimum morale requirements, and failing to meet them forces a player to the rear of the army to recover, causing them to lose the round ( 01:06:00 ).

• Encounter Initiation: Cambrian Archers : Pablo Barros presented the first encounter involving five Cambrian archers. The encounter intensity was rolled at 18, and the group collectively decided to adopt a reckless stance, which dictates they will be in the fight for three rounds ( 01:07:24 ).

• Defensive Maneuvers : Pablo Barros explained the options for defensive maneuvers against the archers' incoming arrows. Players can raise a shield to add plus 10 to their defense roll or perform a zigzag maneuver by rolling their movement skill against the attack ( 01:10:37 ). Pablo Barros clarified that choosing a defensive maneuver means players cannot attack during that round ( 01:13:45 ).

• Damage and Armor Mechanics : Pablo Barros explained that if an arrow strikes, a 1D6 roll determines if the damage is applied to the horse (three or less) or the rider

(more than three). Enrico America questioned the damage taken by their horse, and Pablo Barros confirmed that horses do not heal during the night and that armor points reduce the incoming damage ( 01:15:59 ) (01:19:29 ).

• Initial Combat Outcomes : Laura Triglia failed a horsemanship skill check while attempting to zigzag, causing their horse to get stuck and take damage, though they successfully avoided falling off ( 01:22:14 ). Enrico America's horse also took 9 damage after a failed defensive roll, while Quenhild successfully blocked an arrow using a shield ( 01:19:29 ).

• Archer Encounter Resolution : The group engaged the archers using lances and long weapons. Enrico America successfully killed an archer with a contus, benefiting from a plus 15 bonus, and performed a horsemanship check to stop their horse (01:24:43 ). Pietro Gravino and Laura Triglia continued their attacks, with Pietro Gravino landing a critical hit that allowed them to stop immediately next to an opponent ( 01:28:32 ).

• Clarification of Combat Sequences : Enrico America and Pietro Gravino discussed the turn structure, noting that the battle involves a mix of attacks and defensive maneuvers, and that they were reaching the third and final turn of the archery encounter ( 01:34:42 ).

• Charging and Weapon Bonuses : A debate occurred regarding whether bonuses for charging and using long weapons should stack ( 01:37:32 ). Enrico America and Pietro Gravino argued that they should receive a plus 10 bonus for charging with a long weapon against foot opponents, and Pablo Barros conceded that everyone using a long weapon for a charge receives this total bonus ( 01:38:36 ).

• Finalizing Archer Encounter : The players killed all five archers, and Pablo Barros awarded them a morale recovery of 1D3 for being reckless ( 01:43:25 ). Following the encounter, the group opted to loot the archers' long bows, which Pablo Barros added to their inventory ( 01:44:44 ).

• Encounter Initiation: Knights of Lothian : Pablo Barros introduced a new encounter against five fully armored knights on horses who were ready to charge ( 01:45:32 ). The group discussed their approach, with Enrico America and Laura Triglia debating between adopting a prudent stance or a valorous one ( 01:46:38 ).

• Tactical Strategy Planning : The participants discussed the implications of their stance choice, noting that a prudent stance involves one round of combat but results in additional morale loss ( 01:49:16 ). Laura Triglia and Pietro Gravino questioned the viability of charging against armored knights, but the group

ultimately decided to coordinate their attacks by focusing fire on specific targets to maximize their chances of success ( 01:52:55 ).

• Combat Execution : The group finalized a plan to charge the knights in pairs, with Pietro Gravino and Laura Triglia targeting one knight, and Enrico America and Quenhild targeting another ( 01:55:31 ). Pablo Barros confirmed this approach and prepared to resolve the attacks based on the combined bonuses for charging and long weapons ( 01:56:31 ).

• Combat Mechanics and Charge Bonuses : Pablo Barros, Enrico America, and Pietro Gravino discussed the tactical application of charge bonuses, noting a plus 10 bonus for charging. They clarified that long weapons provide specific advantages during an attack ( 01:57:29 ).

• Combat Resolution and Falling Damage : The group resolved attacks against an opponent, noting that falling damage was applied after the opponent fell from their horse (02:00:39 ). Pablo Barros confirmed that falling damage, totaling 7 points in this instance, is not mitigated by armor ( 02:01:54 ).

• Tactical Movement and Positioning : The group discussed tactical movement following an attack. Pablo Barros clarified that combat actions, such as maneuvers, must be declared prior to execution to remain valid during the battle sequence (02:01:54 ).

• Morale and Recovery : Due to entering the battle prudently, the group suffered a morale penalty of one three -sided die ( 02:05:36 ). They discussed recovery mechanics, noting that characters and their horses could recover health through successful squire rolls ( 02:07:05 ).

• Narrative Developments and Prince Gawain's Arrival : Pablo Barros narrated that Count Sannan retreated, which boosted the group's morale ( 02:10:48 ). Subsequently, Prince Gawain appeared and challenged the group to a "Clash of Champions," an event the group accepted to face him ( 02:12:18 ).

• Clash of Champions Strategy : The group deliberated on the strategy for the duel, noting that such clashes are significant for Saxon warriors ( 02:16:39 ). They debated nominating a champion, with Pietro Gravino and Enrico America emphasizing the importance of strategy over risking a leader's life ( 02:18:10 ).

• Stance and Action Selection : For the duel against Prince Gawain, the group evaluated stance options, ultimately choosing a "valorous" stance for the fourth

round of battle ( 02:21:08 ). They synchronized their actions for the engagement, with Pietro Gravino deciding to charge ( 02:22:18 ).

• Duel Resolution : During the first round of the duel, both parties charged; Pietro Gravino successfully struck Prince Gawain, dealing 1 point of damage after accounting for the opponent's armor ( 02:25:03 ). The participants moved to a second round of engagement ( 02:26:35 ).

• Conclusion of the Champion's Duel : In the second round, the combatants attacked with swords. Pietro Gravino successfully landed an attack, but the opponent's defensive parrying absorbed the damage, ending the duel without further morale loss for the group ( 02:28:00 ).

• Arrival of King Ban and New Encounter Selection : King Ban arrived at the battlefield, providing a morale boost ( 02:29:44 ). Following this, the group was given the opportunity to choose their next encounter and selected the pikemen (02:31:05 ).

• Tactical Strategy Against Pikemen : The group discussed the hazards of charging pikemen, who can set their weapons to counter charges ( 02:34:32 ). They debated using ranged weapons versus a direct charge, eventually deciding to charge, acknowledging the inherent risks to their horses ( 02:36:59 ).

• Execution of Charges Against Pikemen : During the engagement, the group successfully executed their charges ( 02:38:54 ). Laura Triglia and Pietro Gravino reported successful damage rolls, resulting in the elimination of their targets (02:40:10 ) (02:47:07 ).

• Finalizing the Pikemen Encounter : In the second turn of combat against the pikemen, the group successfully engaged and eliminated the remaining opponents. Pietro Gravino noted that their success allowed them to clear the immediate threat (02:44:01 ) (02:47:07 ).

• Post-Battle Celebrations : With King Lot’s forces retreating, the battle concluded. The aftermath involved celebrations and a victory mass held by Arthur, where the group received recognition for their contributions ( 02:49:46 ).

• Glory Point Allocation : Pablo Barros calculated the glory rewards for the group, assigning 45 points for initial participation, with additional points for specific kills, rescue efforts, and the surrender of a prisoner ( 02:51:11 ). It was agreed that the prisoner reward would be split among the five members ( 02:53:56 ).

• Character Sheet Maintenance : Toward the end of the meeting, the group addressed technical issues regarding their character sheets, specifically identifying and removing incorrect "winter phase" entries that had been added during testing (02:55:19 ).

• Battle of Badgrain - Day Two Participation : The participants received 60 points for participation on the second day of the battle. Tamura, acting as the Conroy leader, received double these points. The group earned additional points for defeating specific combatants, including 10 points for killin g pikemen, five points for Adios, and 15 points for Quinn He ( 02:57:29 ).

• Battle of Badgrain - Rewards and Titles : For their efforts, the group was awarded 200 glory for fulfilling Arthur's quest to deliver a message to Leo Grounds. Tamura was granted the title of queen of a small kingdom, earning 1,000 glory. Arthur distributed 20 pounds to each member from the plun der seized from King's Lot's army (02:58:38 ). Financial and Land Grants : Arthur granted A_Adios, Quenhild, and Lynel small parcels of land, providing an income of two pounds per year. Tamura’s kingdom provided an income of five pounds per year. Pablo Barros noted that two pounds per year is the minimum required to support a k night and their squire ( 03:01:58 ).

The companions prepare their equipment and strategy while Merlin seeks Ban’s aid.
The mounted fighters defeat the Cambrian archers and charge the knights of Lothian.
